item.description:
Every piece gets a colophon.

  • The colophon replaces Details: a panel on the reader’s right edge, opened with the new “i” beside Aa or with ⌘I.
  • It has the piece’s cover and title (click to rename), then the work itself: author, year, publisher, ISBN, language and length, edited in place.
  • Below that, the piece in your library: category, kind and tags, when you saved it, how far you are, and how many highlights and notes it has. Then its file or original link.
  • New books bring their publisher, ISBN and language with them. PDFs named with their ISBN keep it, and articles keep their language.
  • Highlighting the start of an opening paragraph no longer shrinks its large first letter, and the selection now shows over it.
  • Highlights that end at the end of a paragraph, or run across two, are now tinted all the way through.
  • Quotes in Marginalia and Highlights leave out footnote markers: “Text¹ blah” is kept as “Text blah”.
  • “Put on the stack” in Save now decides for articles too. They used to go on the stack whatever it said.

A welcome for a brand new library.

  • Opening Scribe with nothing saved now begins with a short welcome: books settle onto a shelf, then three quick steps. Tell Scribe your name, choose how the page looks, and save something to read.
  • Anything you save during the welcome carries on saving after it, with its progress in the top bar.
  • Settings ▸ Updates & about has Show welcome, to see it again.
  • Today no longer shows its empty-library greeting for a moment while a full library loads.

Scribe says hello, saves many things at once, and the Aa panel slides instead of stepping.

  • Tell Scribe your name in Settings, under You, and Today greets you: good morning, afternoon or evening, “Reading late?” after ten, “A new week” on Monday mornings, and “Welcome back” after a long break. Turn it off there too.
  • A brand new library gets a proper welcome on Today: a greeting, a field to paste your first link into, and outlines where your first books will go.
  • Save is one screen now: paste a link at the top, or drop files below. No more tabs.
  • Paste several links at once, one per line, or choose or drop many PDFs and EPUBs, or a whole folder of them. Each is saved in turn, with its progress shown.
  • Close the Save sheet and saving carries on. A “Saving 2 of 5” pill in the top bar shows how it’s going and opens the list again.
  • Anything that couldn’t be saved stays in the list with the reason, and a Retry button.
  • Drop a PDF, an EPUB, a folder or a web link anywhere on Scribe’s window to save it.
  • “Put on the stack” sends what you save straight to your stack instead of the backlog.
  • PDFs whose own title is a leftover from the software that made them, such as “Design” or “370848_Print.indd”, are named after the file instead, tidied up: no ISBN, no author list, and the colon put back.
  • Column width and line spacing are sliders now, so you can set them anywhere between narrow and wide, snug and airy.
  • A new Weight slider makes the text lighter or darker. It suits evening reading, and works with the Serif and Sans faces.
  • Justify gives paragraphs even edges, hyphenated like a printed page.
  • Reset, beside Typeface, puts everything back to Scribe’s own settings.
  • Weight and Justify are in Settings too, under Reading.
